arguments.command:
python -c "
import parse

# Test cases that should raise errors
tests_should_error = [
    '{abc',           # unclosed brace
    'test}',          # unmatched close
    'abc{def',        # prefix + unclosed
    'abc}def',        # prefix + unmatched close
]

# Test cases that should work
tests_should_work = [
    ('{name}', 'hello'),
    ('{{ }}', ' { }'),
    ('{name:w}', 'hello world'),
    ('text {name} more', 'text hello more'),
    ('{hello.world}', 'a_b_c'.split('_')[0]),
    ('{{', '{{'),
    ('}}', '}}'),
]

print('=== Tests that SHOULD ERROR ===')
for t in tests_should_error:
    try:
        result = parse.Parser(t)
        print(f'  {t!r}: NO ERROR (BAD!)')
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f'  {t!r}: ValueError raised (GOOD)')
    except Exception as e:
        print(f'  {t!r}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}')

print()
print('=== Tests that SHOULD WORK ===')
for fmt, val in tests_should_work:
    try:
        parser = parse.Parser(fmt)
        result = parser.parse(val) if '{' not in fmt or fmt == '{{' else None
        print(f'  {fmt!r}: OK (expression: {parser._expression!r})')
    except Exception as e:
        print(f'  {fmt!r}: {type(e).__name__}: {e} (BAD!)')
" 2>&1
